Neoplasm arising in or involving the iris.
Polyclonal excess of circulating immunoglobulins is a blood protein abnormality; underlying liver disease, infection or autoimmunity does not establish additional organ involvement.
Spinal cord/meningeal protrusion through a vertebral defect; neurogenic bladder causes urinary tract dysfunction in most (~70-90%) open cases.
Inherited thyroid hormone synthesis defect causing congenital hypothyroidism; other listed manifestations are occasional or transient.
Immune-mediated inflammatory demyelinating peripheral neuropathy; familial predisposition does not change the affected organ.

Fat malabsorption caused by exocrine pancreatic dysfunction; no endocrine pancreatic disease is specified.
Neoplasms originating in the heart, pericardium or vessels.
Cerebellar degeneration with cognitive impairment; testicular atrophy and azoospermia are reproductive findings without documented hormonal dysfunction.
Corneal dystrophy, keratoderma and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; enamel defects and carious teeth occur in 80-99%; hearing impairment is only 5-29%.
Skeletal dysplasia; hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%. Sleep apnea is separately diagnosed; singleton pulmonary hypoplasia does not establish common involvement.
Demyelinating peripheral neuropathy; progressive denervation causes distal muscle wasting and foot deformity in most patients (>30%).
Reflex epilepsy triggered by orgasm; the trigger does not imply reproductive organ disease.
Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy; intellectual disability and impaired speech occur in 30-79%; biliary atresia is only 5-29%.
Congenital bilateral bony fusion between the humerus and ulna.
Clonal hematopoietic neoplasm with JAK2 rearrangement; lymphoma is not the defining or predominant presentation across this category.
Familial abnormal retrograde urine flow from bladder into ureters; the urinary tract is within the renal axis.
Progressive cerebellar disease and erythrokeratoderma define the syndrome; nystagmus and impaired pursuit are neurologic signs rather than intrinsic eye damage.
Cardiomyopathy with defining keratoderma and woolly hair; skin findings are strongly supported by phenotype counts despite variable penetrance.
Alopecia, skeletal contractures/fusions and intellectual disability define the syndrome; myopia occurs in 30-79%; dental enamel defects (30-79%) omitted by the four-axis cap.
